chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Fuḍayl Sukkarah, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be your ransom, is there a fixed limit for water?

He said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to ʿAlī عليه السلام: ‘When I die, draw for me six water-skins from the water of the well of Ghars, and wash me and shroud me. Then when you have finished my washing and my shrouding, take hold of the ends of my shroud and seat me up, then ask me whatever you wish, for by Allah, you will not ask me about anything except that I will answer you regarding it.’”

key_terms.أَجَبْتُكَ: I would answer you, indicating a promised response to questioning
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, asked about here in relation to a defined quantity
key_terms.بِئْرِ غَرْسٍ: the well of Ghars, the source of the water mentioned
key_terms.حَدٌّ مَحْدُودٌ: a fixed, specified limit or measure
key_terms.سِتَّ قِرَبٍ: six water-skins, the stated quantity of water to be drawn
key_terms.غَسِّلْنِي: wash me, referring to the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.كَفَنِي: my shroud, the burial cloth of the deceased
key_terms.كَفِّنِّي: shroud me, referring to wrapping the deceased in a kafan

ai.seo_question: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم specify a set amount of water for his ghusl after death?
ai.summary: This hadith records a question to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام about whether water has a defined limit, and he answers by citing an instruction of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding the amount of water to be drawn for his ghusl after death. The narration also conveys a unique prophetic instruction concerning the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم state after washing and shrouding, highlighting his special rank and the transmission of knowledge to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام.
